notes: Identity assessment: the supplied canonical text identifies the matching title and all four authors (Toman Barsbai, Hillel Rapoport, Andreas Steinmayr, Christoph Trebesch). Its cover says "No 2016-26 – September" and "Working Paper", and its provenance URL is https://www.cepii.fr/PDF_PUB/wp/2016/wp2016-26.pdf. This is an author primary working-paper report with body, tables and appendix through printed page 59, not the cited 2017 AEJ Applied Economics 9(3), 36–69 journal version. The cited DOI is not printed in the supplied text; equivalence to the final publication is unverified. No PDF was supplied. Both assigned rows have null descriptions/study identifiers and empty locators; no row-specific target can be independently identified. Candidate evidence only, identical across rows without assigning either row to a coefficient: Table 1, printed p. 37, column 3 gives westward-emigration OLS coefficient -0.63 (SE 0.18), marked ***, and eastward-emigration OLS coefficient 0.39 (SE 0.16), marked **. Its legend supplies significance bounds at 1% and 5%, respectively; no exact p is assigned. The same table has other specifications, destinations and opposition-party outcomes. Table 2 (p. 38) varies election years and mayor outcomes; Table 3 (p. 39) varies subsamples. Table 4 (p. 40) gives individual political outcomes with 5,480 or 8,350 observations, and Table 5 (p. 41) exit-poll outcomes with 7,344, 1,194, 2,327 or 3,051 observations depending on column. These are alternative analytic samples, not mutually exclusive groups to sum. Table 1 candidate model N=848 is communities, with district-clustered standard errors, not participants or districts; out-of-country votes and Transnistria are excluded from the empirical analysis. N=848 is retained only as a model candidate for parent field-scope review. No N arithmetic, conversion, df inference, or target allocation by row order/numeric matching was performed.
